title: Mabel Mercer, Billie Holiday and great voices as models of sound
summary: With Fisher he talks about Mabel Mercer's effect on audiences, missing her on 52nd Street, and Billie Holiday's debt to her.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Mabel Mercer. Mabel Mercer scared me to death.
Yeah. Well she's so gorgeous. When did you first hear her?
Very first and only time it was just about five - six years ago.
Woman could not sing a note, you know, couldn't sing a note and just bring you to tears in an instant man.
That's heart...make you cry, make you stand up, make you do anything.
Most amazing singer, I think, I've ever seen.
Utterly amazing. Brought me, literally, to tears.

You see, up on 52nd Street I missed her because I was over on the other side of the street. She was up at Tony's and I wasn't aware of Tony's. I was young and I listened to all the saxophone players, you know, on this end. Tatum and everybody. If I'd have just had the presence of mind or if somebody would have said something to me, I could have walked up the street in 1946 and heard her then. So she told me Billie Holiday used to come up there and listen to her. I know that Billie got a lot of stuff from her, with that sophistication and she said the boss
had to come up and get mad (at Billie) and tell her to come back and do her job. Hahahaha. Yeah.
So this is what I got together. So I figured that I'd go along with them and put all them together and, consequently, maybe Nick will come out. You know. Yeah. Hahahaha. Come on out of there.
